First listed 2026-10-07 · episode or wrap

The AI Bull Case with Joseph Carlson

Carlson argues AI utility and incumbent distribution support a bullish hyperscaler case, especially Meta, while distinguishing software with embedded workflows from tax and travel intermediaries. Eisman accepts utility but questions model moats and capital returns. Meta results support growth and adoption, not proof of full AI investment payback. Apple documents contradict a necessary customer-data transfer to Google. Most company disruption theses remain unverified; the six-month agentic-commerce forecast has an unfinished horizon.

Substack · 2026-10-07 ↗
The episode usefully separates useful technology from investor returns and differentiates company exposure. Strong strategic assertions about moats, software disruption, product superiority and Apple dependence need more evidence. Eisman does not adopt every guest thesis merely by summarizing it.
